name: Confusion
description: Confusion in elderly patients refers to an acute or subacute change in mental status characterised by disorientation, impaired attention, and altered consciousness. Acute confusion (delirium) is a medical emergency that must be distinguished from dementia (which is chronic and progressive). Common precipitants in older adults include infection (especially urinary tract infection, pneumonia), metabolic disturbances (hypo/hyperglycaemia, hyponatraemia, uraemia), medication effects (anticholinergics, opioids, benzodiazepines), pain, constipation, and urinary retention. The '4 A's Test' (4AT) or Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) are validated bedside tools for delirium screening.
